questions.question: Which of the following is the only floating national park in India and the world?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Keibul Lamjao National Park.

Key Points

  • Keibul Lamjao National Park: 
    • It is a national park in the Bishnupur district of the state of Manipur in India.
    • The national park is characterized by many floating decomposed plant materials locally called phumdis.
    • The park which was initially declared to be a sanctuary in 1966, was subsequently declared to be a national park in 1977 through a gazette notification.
    • Kishtwar National Park is a national park located in the Kishtwar district of Jammu and Kashmir, India.
    • Khangchendzonga National Park also Kanchenjunga Biosphere Reserve is a National Park and a Biosphere reserve located in Sikkim, India.
    • Khirganga National Park is a national park in Himachal Pradesh, India established in 2010.
    • Jim Corbett National Park is a forested wildlife sanctuary in northern India’s Uttarakhand State.

Additional Information

Gugamal National Park Gugamal National Park is an Indian national park that is one of seven protected areas in the Melghat Tiger Reserve. Founded on 22 February 1974, this park is located in the Chikhaldara and Dharni tehsils of Amravati, Maharashtra.
Nagarhole National Park It is also known as Rajiv Gandhi National Park, which is a wildlife reserve in the South Indian state of Karnataka. Part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, the park is backed by the Brahamagiri Mountains and filled with sandalwood and teak trees.
Balpakram National Park It is a national park in the south of Garo Hills in Meghalaya, India, located at an altitude of about 910 m close to the international border with Bangladesh.

questions.question: In which state is the Gorumara National Park located?

questions.question: Which national park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is home to species like Megapode, crab-eating Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and Giant Robber Crab?
questions.questionHtml: Which national park in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is home to species like Megapode, crab-eating Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and Giant Robber Crab?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Campbell Bay National Park.

Key Points

  • Campbell Bay National Park is located on the Great Nicobar Island, which is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
  • The park is known for its rich biodiversity and is home to unique species such as the Megapode, crab-eating Macaque, Nicobar Pigeon, and Giant Robber Crab.
  • It covers an area of approximately 426 square kilometers, making it one of the largest national parks in the region.
  • The park's diverse ecosystems include tropical evergreen forests, mangroves, and coastal habitats, which provide a sanctuary for various flora and fauna.

Additional Information

  • Megapode
    • The Megapode is a unique bird found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
    • It is known for its distinctive nesting behavior, where it builds large mounds of earth and vegetation to incubate its eggs.
    • The heat generated from the decomposing vegetation within the mound provides the necessary warmth for the eggs to hatch.
  • Crab-eating Macaque
    • The crab-eating Macaque, also known as the long-tailed Macaque, is a primate species native to Southeast Asia.
    • It is called the crab-eating Macaque because of its diet, which includes crabs, fruits, and small animals.
    • These Macaques are known for their adaptability and can thrive in various habitats, including coastal regions and forests.
  • Nicobar Pigeon
    • The Nicobar Pigeon is a large, colorful bird found in the Nicobar Islands and other parts of Southeast Asia.
    • It is known for its iridescent plumage, which displays a range of metallic colors.
    • The Nicobar Pigeon is the closest living relative of the extinct dodo bird.
  • Giant Robber Crab
    • The Giant Robber Crab, also known as the coconut crab, is the largest terrestrial arthropod in the world.
    • It is known for its ability to climb trees and crack open coconuts with its powerful claws.
    • The crab is primarily nocturnal and is found in coastal regions and forests of the Indo-Pacific islands.

questions.question: In which state of India is the Tadoba National Park located?
questions.questionHtml: In which state of India is the Tadoba National Park located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

Key Points

  • Tadoba National Park is located in the Chandrapur district of Maharashtra.
  • It is also known as Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve, which is the largest and oldest national park in Maharashtra.
  • The park was established in 1955 and covers an area of approximately 1,727 square kilometers.
  • Tadoba National Park is famous for its significant population of Bengal tigers and is a prominent destination for wildlife enthusiasts and photographers.

Additional Information

  • National Parks in India
    • National parks are protected areas established by the government for the conservation of wildlife and biodiversity.
    • India is home to a diverse range of national parks, each offering unique habitats and species.
    • Some other famous national parks in India include Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand, Kaziranga National Park in Assam, and Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan.
    • These parks play a crucial role in the conservation of endangered species and serve as important research and education centers.
  • Tiger Reserves in India
    • India is home to more than 50 tiger reserves, which are established under the Project Tiger initiative launched in 1973.
    • Tiger reserves aim to protect and increase the population of Bengal tigers in the country.
    • These reserves provide a safe habitat for tigers and other wildlife, while also promoting eco-tourism and community involvement in conservation efforts.
    • The Tadoba Andhari Tiger Reserve is one of the most popular and successful tiger reserves in India.
  • Biodiversity in Maharashtra
    • Maharashtra is a state with rich biodiversity, encompassing various ecosystems such as forests, grasslands, and coastal regions.
    • The state is home to several national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and conservation reserves.
    • In addition to Tadoba National Park, other notable protected areas in Maharashtra include Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Navegaon National Park, and Melghat Tiger Reserve.
    • The state's diverse flora and fauna contribute to its ecological significance and attract nature enthusiasts from around the world.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct I– Maximum National Parks in India are located in the state of Madhya Pradesh. II – Mudumalai National Park is located in Kerala. III – The Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History is located in Tamil Nadu.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements is/are correct

I– Maximum National Parks in India are located in the state of Madhya Pradesh.

II – Mudumalai National Park is located in Kerala.

III – The Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History is located in Tamil Nadu.

options.text: Both I and II are correct
options.html: Both I and II are correct

options.text: Both I and III are correct
options.html: Both I and III are correct

questions.solution: Madhya Pradesh has the highest number of national parks in India, including notable ones like Kanha, Bandhavgarh, and Pench. The Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History, named after renowned ornithologist Dr. Salim Ali, is located in Tamil Nadu. Mudumalai National Park, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, is situated at the tri-junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, but it is actually located in Tamil Nadu. Thus, the correct statements are that Madhya Pradesh has the maximum national parks and the Salim Ali Centre is in Tamil Nadu.

questions.questionHtml: ________ Tiger reserve in Karnataka is home to the largest number of Asian elephants in the world.
questions.solution: Distributed throughout Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent, the Asian elephant is the largest land animal species in Asia. It has been listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List and currently has an estimated population of 40,000 to 50,000. About half of this population is reported to be in India, mainly the Nagarhole Tiger Reserve which is located in the Mysore district of Karnataka.

questions.question: In which of the following protected areas in India the human interference is prohibited?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following protected areas in India the human interference is prohibited?
questions.solution: National Park is a protected area reserved for the protection of only animals, where no human intervention is allowed. Interference in any form, timber harvesting, the collection of minor forest products and private property rights is completely prohibited. Whereas a wildlife sanctuary is a protected area reserved for the conservation of only animals and human activities such as timber harvesting, and the collection of minor forestry is allowed.

questions.question: The Uttar Pradesh cabinet approved a proposal to name a zoological garden at ________ after the freedom fighter and revolutionary Ashfaqullah Khan.
questions.questionHtml: The Uttar Pradesh cabinet approved a proposal to name a zoological garden at ________ after the freedom fighter and revolutionary Ashfaqullah Khan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gorakhpur.

Key Points

  • Recently, the Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved a proposal to set up a zoological garden in Gorakhpur on 121 acres.
  • A plan to set aside Rs 234 crore for the development of a zoological garden named after Shaheed Ashfaqullah Khan was approved by the Uttar Pradesh state government on 8 January 2020.
  • It aims to attract tourists and to increase employment opportunities.

Additional Information 

  • Ashfaqulla Khan was a freedom fighter in the Indian independence movement.
  • He was born on 22 October 1900 in Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh.
  • He participated in Gandhi's non-cooperation movement (NCM), Chauri Chaura incident.
  • Ashfaqulla Khan formed the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) along with Ram Prasad Bismil.
  • At present, there are two zoological gardens in Uttar Pradesh namely:
    • Nawab Wajid Ali Shah Zoological Garden in Lucknow
    • Kanpur Zoological Park in Kanpur

questions.question: Which of the following places/regions is the natural habitat of the Indian wild ass?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following places/regions is the natural habitat of the Indian wild ass?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Little Rann of Kutch.

Key Points

  • Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary, sometimes referred to as the Wild Ass Wildlife Sanctuary, is situated in India's Gujarat state in the Little Rann of Kutch.
  • The Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 was the legal basis on which the wildlife sanctuary was created.
  • The sanctuary is where it is possible to see the critically endangered Indian Wild Ass (Khur) subspecies of the Asiatic Wild Ass species Onager (Equus hemionus).
  • The main threat faced by the sanctuary is the illegal salt panning activity in the area.
  • 25% of India’s salt supply comes from panning activity in the area.

Additional Information

  • Sunderbans:
    • The Sundarbans is of universal importance for endangered species including the Royal Bengal Tiger, Ganges and Irawadi dolphins, estuarine crocodiles.
  • Upper Himalayas:
    • The Himalayan Range's tallest mountains are known as the Great Himalayas, Greater Himalayas, or Himadri.
    • The Greater Himalayas mountain range includes Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, as well as other "nearest highest" peaks like Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, and Nanga Parbat.
  • Plains of Ganga:
    • Large floodplains of the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra river systems are collectively referred to as the Indus-Ganga plains, commonly referred to as the "Great Plains."

questions.question: Which of the following is the first national park that was established in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the first national park that was established in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jim Corbett, National ParkKey Points

  • ​Jim Corbett National Park is the first national park in India
  • Jim Corbett National Park is located in the Nainital district of Uttarakhand, India.
  • It was established in the year 1936, making it India's oldest national park.
  • The park was originally named Hailey National Park, after Sir Malcolm Hailey, the Governor of the United Provinces at the time.
  • It was later renamed after Jim Corbett, a renowned naturalist, conservationist, and former tiger hunter.
  • The primary purpose of the park is to protect endangered Bengal tigers, as it was the first to come under the Project Tiger initiative in 1973.​
  • The park is now over 1,300 square kilometers in size and has a variety of flora and fauna. 
  • A national park is a protected area that is designed to protect and develop wildlife and its environment.
  • As of January 2023, India has 106 national parks that cover 1.35% of the country's geographical area. 

Additional Information

  •  Gir National Park
    • It is located in Gujarat
    • Established: 1965
    • Famous for: The only habitat of the Asiatic Lions in the world.
    • Significance: Plays a vital role in conserving Asiatic Lions and supports a diverse ecosystem including leopards, antelopes, and crocodiles.
  • Kaziranga National Park
    • It is located in Assam
    • Established: 1905 (as a reserve forest, declared a national park in 1974).
    • Famous for: The one-horned rhinoceros, which constitutes the largest population of this species in the world.
    • Significance: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, it also supports tigers, elephants, and swamp deer, forming part of the Big Five of Kaziranga.
  • Rajaji National Park
    • It is located inUttarakhand
    • Established: 1983
    • Famous for: Its population of Asian elephants and other wildlife, including leopards and tigers.
    • Significance: Located in the Shivalik range, it is known for its diverse flora and fauna and serves as an important wildlife corridor.

questions.question: Under which of the following Articles can a person directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of his Fundamental Rights?
questions.questionHtml: Under which of the following Articles can a person directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of his Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 32.

Key Points

  • Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
  • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution, emphasizing its importance in upholding fundamental rights.
  • Article 32 guarantees the right to constitutional remedies, empowering the Supreme Court to issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for the enforcement of these rights.
  • This provision ensures that the fundamental rights are not merely theoretical but can be practically enforced through the highest court in India.
  • Any individual whose fundamental rights are violated can directly approach the Supreme Court without having to go through lower courts first.

Additional Information

  • Fundamental Rights
    • These are a set of rights granted to all citizens by the Indian Constitution, aimed at ensuring individual liberty and equality.
    • There are six fundamental rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
  • Writs
    • Habeas Corpus: A writ requiring a person to be brought before a judge or court, especially to secure the person's release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention.
    • Mandamus: A writ issued as a command to an inferior court or ordering a person to perform a public or statutory duty.
    • Prohibition: A writ directing a subordinate to stop doing something the law prohibits.
    • Quo Warranto: A writ requiring a person to show by what warrant an office or franchise is held, claimed, or exercised.
    • Certiorari: A writ by which a higher court reviews a case tried in a lower court.
  • Judicial Review
    • The power of the judiciary to review and determine the validity of a law or an order.
    • It helps in upholding the supremacy of the Constitution and ensuring the protection of fundamental rights.
  • Supreme Court of India
    • The apex judicial body in India, established in 1950.
    • It has the power to interpret the Constitution and enforce the fundamental rights of citizens.
    • The decisions of the Supreme Court are binding on all courts within India.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Corbett National Park located?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following states is the Corbett National Park located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

Key Points

  • The Jim Corbett National Park, which is a part of the larger Corbett Tiger Reserve, a Project Tiger Reserve lies in the Nainital district of Uttarakhand.
  • On 8th August 1936, India’s first national park was established as Hailey National Park.
    • It was named after the then Governor of the United Provinces, British India, Sir Malcolm Hailey.
  • It is also Asia’s first national park.
  • It was renamed Ramganga National Park in 1954-55 and again renamed Corbett National Park in 1955-56.
  • When the Government of India launched Project Tiger in 1973, the park became a part of this project.
